### Lemma 1

Let a finite planar set have diameter `D`, and let `vx_-`, `vx_+` be distinct
actual diameter edges. Let `u` lie strictly between the oriented rays from `v`
to `x_-` and `x_+`. Orient `Ju` so that

\[
(x_--v)\cdot Ju<0<(x_+-v)\cdot Ju.
\]

Two disjoint proper crosscuts divide the outer-face disk into coarse layers
`L,M,R`. Suppose `v` lies in `L` and both `x_-`, `x_+` lie in `R` (the reversed
case is identical). Thus both witness edges cross both cuts.

For every diameter edge with exactly one endpoint `z` in `M`, orient its vector
`n` toward `z`. Each of the two middle boundary arcs has one fixed, strict sign
of `n dot Ju`, shared by every moving diameter endpoint on that arc. The signs
on the two arcs are opposite whenever both arcs contain moving diameter endpoints.

## 10. Compact handoff

```text
FAQ fixed-angle quadrilateral theorem:
Let a convex diameter-one quadrilateral have AC=BD=1 and diagonal angle
phi in [pi/3,2pi/3]. Then
  P <= P4(phi)
     =2+sqrt(2-sqrt(3)sin phi-cos phi)
        +sqrt(2-sqrt(3)sin phi+cos phi).

Proof: write B in the intersection of the four unit disks centered at
0,e,v,e+v. The perimeter is the convex sum of distances to those four centers,
so maximize on the boundary. On a boundary circle whose adjacent-center angle is
psi in [pi/3,2pi/3], feasibility restricts t to [psi-pi/3,pi/3]. Centering at
x=t-psi/2 gives
  F(x)=1+4sin(psi/4)cos(x/2)+sqrt(1+4C^2-4C cos x), C=cos(psi/2).
A direct derivative calculation reduces F'(x)>0 for x>0 to
  4C^3+8C cos^2(x/2)-3C-1>0,
whose minimum on the allowed rectangle is sqrt(3)>0. Thus the maximum is an arc
endpoint, yielding the formula above. Endpoints are feasible.

Equality forces three quadrilateral vertices pairwise at distance one. Hence Target C
C15 excludes exact equality for sufficiently large minimizers.

At phi_c=p_c/2:
  P4(phi_c)=3.034910765287770...,
  p_c-P4(phi_c)=0.00040155411620747....
Next: quantitative nested-convex area penalty for adding that missing perimeter.
```

### Theorem FAQ — fixed-angle small quadrilateral

Let `ABCD` be a nondegenerate convex quadrilateral of diameter at most one whose two diagonals satisfy

\[
AC=BD=1.
\]

Let

\[
\phi\in[\pi/3,2\pi/3]
\]

be the smaller oriented angle between the diagonal lines. Then

\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{per}(ABCD)
\le P_4(\phi),
}
\tag{FAQ.1}

where

\[
\boxed{
P_4(\phi)
:=
2+
\sqrt{2-\sqrt3\sin\phi-\cos\phi}
+
\sqrt{2-\sqrt3\sin\phi+\cos\phi}.
}
\tag{FAQ.2}

Equality is attained. Every equality configuration has a three-vertex equilateral triangle of side one among the four quadrilateral vertices.

The function is symmetric under

\[
\phi\mapsto\pi-\phi.
\]

At `phi=pi/2`, FAQ.2 becomes

\[
2+2\sqrt{2-\sqrt3}
=2+\sqrt6-\sqrt2,
\]

recovering Tamvakis's maximal unit-diameter quadrilateral perimeter.

At the HKS angle

\[
\phi_c:=p_c/2
=1.5176561597019888\ldots,
\]

FAQ gives

\[
\boxed{
P_4(\phi_c)
=3.0349107652877701707\ldots,
}
\tag{FAQ.3}

so

\[
\boxed{
p_c-P_4(\phi_c)
=0.0004015541162074667\ldots .}
\tag{FAQ.4}

This is more than eleven times the global Tamvakis separation `p_c-P_4^*` used in TQB.

## Theorem

Let \(\mathcal T\) be a family of pairwise disjoint non-singleton global
outer-to-outer stopped trains whose crosscuts lie on one complement-dual path. Assume
all train projective directions lie in an interval \(J\) of width \(W\). Fix a
diameter vertex \(v\), and let \(\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal T\) be a subfamily such
that every train in \(\mathcal L\) is single-star two-sided braced by \(v\) in the
sense of audited Section 157.

Put
\[
a_D=\arcsin\frac1{2D},
\qquad
M(W,D)=2\left(\left\lfloor\frac{W}{2a_D}\right\rfloor+1\right)+1.
\tag{1}
\]

Then there is a subfamily \(\mathcal L'\subseteq\mathcal L\) and two fixed distinct
actual diameter edges
\[
h_+=vx_+,\qquad h_-=vx_-
\]
such that
\[
\boxed{
|\mathcal L'|\ge \frac{|\mathcal L|}{2M(W,D)}
}
\tag{2}
\]
and \(h_+,h_-\) cross every train cut in \(\mathcal L'\) with opposite strict
transverse signs.

For a Section-90 phase shore \(W=4K/D\). Since
\[
2a_D=2\arcsin\frac1{2D}\ge\frac1D,
\]
one may take
\[
\boxed{M_K=2\lfloor4K\rfloor+3}
\tag{3}
\]
and obtain
\[
\boxed{
|\mathcal L'|\ge \frac{|\mathcal L|}{2M_K}.
}
\tag{4}
\]

No endpoint limit is used.
